title: The railways took half. Tech takes 28 cents.
sub: One technology's share of every dollar a country invested - Britain's railways at their peak, US computing and software today
src: UK: Campbell & Turner literature (via Focus-Economics) - US: BEA data via FRED, Q2 2026
src_full: Railway ~50%: 'about 50% of the country's entire gross domestic capital formation' (Campbell & Turner literature; Focus-Economics summary), a secondary record in the dossier. US 28: (Y034RC1Q027SBEA + B985RC1Q027SBEA) / GPDI, the railway-yardstick reading of 2026-08-30 for 2026 Q2 (28.184%), written as the whole cent the script and the yardstick page both state.

proof.quote: more than 6.5% of national income and about 50% of the country's entire gross domestic capital formation. Source: Campbell & Turner literature; Focus-Economics summary.

information-processing equipment + software / GPDI | (Y034RC1Q027SBEA + B985RC1Q027SBEA) / GPDI ... the railway 50% was ONE technology against Britain's total capital formation. Neither US line is single-technology
Today it's twenty-eight, the most it has ever been. In the 1840s railways took roughly half of everything Britain invested

provenance_note: P69 T14a (2026-09-22). Tier PLAUSIBLE: the 28 is CONFIRMED (a primary FRED reading on disk), the railway 50 is secondary only (the dossier's summary of the Campbell & Turner literature; no primary on disk), and a series takes its weakest figure's tier. The two denominators differ (Britain's gross domestic capital formation; US gross private domestic investment) - the yardstick README's caveat, and ev-capital-formation-v1 already draws the same 50 as an hline. domain [0, 30] is the scale 28 reads on; the railway bar is the breakthrough (E60, CAPABILITIES 'The BREAKTHROUGH bars'), per REBUILD-TREATMENT-H.md row 14.
